architecture.mechanism: Removal/reduction of biodegradable organic precursor load (TOC) through polishing pretreatment so less nutritional substrate reaches the membrane surface, thereby slowing biofilm development and extending intervals between cleanings.
architecture.intervention: Install an anoxic granular-activated-carbon (GAC) biological contactor upstream of the SWRO train (without downstream chlorine addition or residual oxidant), followed by fine filters and anti-scalant dosing only, and implement continuous TOC monitoring with alarm/trip setpoints; replace periodic chlorination-based bio-prevention with this adsorptive/biological carbon polisher plus UV or other non-oxidative disinfection before RO.
architecture.expected_effect: Decrease in biofilm-forming potential entering the RO skids, lengthening CIP intervals toward or beyond quarterly design targets, recovering normalized-flux droop below 15% between cleans, and maintaining plant permeate recovery because feed TDS is not compromised and anti-scalant chemistry is unchanged.
architecture.falsification_test: Run the existing pretreatment train with the GAC biological contactor offline for four weeks under normal feed conditions while matching upstream/downstream flow distribution to the active train, then compare month-over-month transmembrane pressure rise per permeate volume, normalized flux at fixed operating points, and biofilm biomass assays on spare membrane coupons; if the active train does not show statistically significant reductions relative to the bypass run, the mechanism is falsified.
